query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered suitable for thin-film use, and its expense favors applying it as a protective coating on conventional metals rather than using it in bulk. Earlier studies examined room-temperature wear behavior in relation to coating–substrate combinations, composition, and grain size, but largely addressed the alloy itself or a limited thermal regime rather than the overall wear response of a coating across different temperatures. Under the constraints that FeNiCrCoCu remains a thin protective coating and that high-temperature wear is the target application, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs its overall wear resistance and why? Specify an intervention relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the observations expected if the hypothesis is correct, state the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, connect the hypothesis to prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The overall wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin protective coatings on conventional metals is governed by the synergistic effects of coating-substrate interfacial adhesion, grain size refinement, and the formation of a stable oxide layer at elevated temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu thin protective coating on a conventional metal substrate with an average grain size of 10 μm
generation.intervention: Application of a high-temperature annealing treatment (800°C for 1 hour) to enhance coating-substrate interfacial adhesion and promote grain size refinement
generation.conditions: Elevated temperature range (500°C to 900°C) and wear loading conditions (normal load: 10 N, sliding speed: 0.1 m/s)
generation.structural_mediator: Coating-substrate interfacial adhesion and grain size
generation.mechanism: The formation of a stable oxide layer at elevated temperatures, enhanced by improved coating-substrate interfacial adhesion and grain size refinement, which reduces wear rate by minimizing adhesive wear and promoting oxidative wear
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in wear rate compared to the baseline coating condition without annealing treatment, measured in terms of volume loss per unit sliding distance (mm³/m)
generation.baseline: As-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin protective coating on a conventional metal substrate
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 500°C to 900°C, loading conditions: normal load up to 50 N, sliding speed up to 1 m/s
generation.uncertainty: The actual wear resistance may vary depending on the specific coating-substrate combination, composition, and grain size distribution, as well as the presence of other environmental factors such as humidity and contamination

falsification_experiment.design: Reciprocating sliding wear test with a spherical counterbody (6 mm diameter) against the FeNiCrCoCu coated substrate, using a high-temperature tribometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate of the annealed coating is not reduced by at least 20% compared to the baseline coating condition, or if the coefficient of friction increases by more than 10% at any temperature within the specified range, the hypothesis is falsified
